babs.8: May the junub put his hand in the vessel before washing it?
babs.10: One who poured with his right hand onto his left in the bath
babs.11: When one has intercourse and repeats it, and one who went round his wives with a single bath
babs.12: Washing off madhy and ablution because of it
babs.13: One who perfumed himself, then bathed, and the trace of perfume remained
babs.14: Running the fingers through the hair until one thinks the skin is moistened, then pouring water over it
babs.15: One who performed ablution in janāba and then washed the rest of his body
babs.16: When one remembers in the mosque that one is junub: he goes out as he is and does not perform tayammum

248.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he began by washing his hands, then performed ablution as for prayer, then put his fingers into the water and ran them through the roots of his hair, then poured three handfuls over his head with his hands, then let the water flow over all his skin.”
248.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution before the bath.” ʿĀʾisha describes the sequence: first washing the hands, then the prayer ablution, then running the fingers through the roots of the hair, pouring water three times over the head, and finally pouring water over the whole skin. The chain runs through ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf, Mālik, Hishām and his father to ʿĀʾisha.

249.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Maymūna, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, she said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed his ablution for prayer except for his feet, and washed his private part and whatever filth had touched him, then poured water over himself, then moved aside and washed his feet. This was his bath from janāba.”
249.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Ablution before the bath.” Maymūna describes a sequence: prayer ablution without the feet, washing the private part and the filth, pouring water over himself, then moving aside and washing the feet. The wording stresses that this was his bath from janāba.

250.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, from a bowl called al-Faraq.”
250.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man bathing together with his wife.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she and the Prophet bathed from the same vessel, a bowl called al-Faraq. The text gives no further detail on the size of the bowl.

251.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd aṣ-Ṣamad narrated to me, he said: Shuʿba narrated to me, he said: Abū Bakr ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū Salama say: “I and ʿĀʾisha’s brother went in to ʿĀʾisha, and her brother asked her about the bathing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She called for a vessel of about a ṣāʿ, bathed and poured water over her head, with a screen between us and her.” Abū ʿAbdallāh said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī said, from Shuʿba: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”
251.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” When her brother asks about the bathing of the Prophet, ʿĀʾisha has a vessel of about a ṣāʿ brought and bathes behind a screen. Abū ʿAbdallāh (al-Bukhārī) adds the wording of Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”

252.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us: “He was with Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, he and his father, and with him were some people. They asked him about the bath, and he said: A ṣāʿ is enough for you. A man said: It is not enough for me. Jābir said: It was enough for one who had more hair than you and was better than you. Then he led us in prayer in one garment.”
252.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” Asked about the bath, Jābir says a ṣāʿ is enough. To a man for whom it is not enough, he replies that it was enough for one who had more hair and was better; the wording does not name him explicitly. He then led the prayer in one garment.

253.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Maymūna used to bathe from one vessel.” And Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī said, from Shuʿba: “the measure of a ṣāʿ.”
253.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing with a ṣāʿ and the like.” The wording reports that the Prophet and Maymūna bathed from one vessel. The statement “the measure of a ṣāʿ” is added here by Yazīd ibn Hārūn, Bahz and al-Judī through Shuʿba.

254.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad narrated to me, he said: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I pour water over my head three times.” And he gestured with both his hands.
254.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” The Prophet says he pours water over his head three times and gestures with both hands. The chain runs through Abū Nuʿaym, Zuhayr, Abū Isḥāq and Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad to Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.

255.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Mukhawwal ibn Rāshid, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pour water over his head three times.”
255.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” Jābir reports briefly that the Prophet poured water over his head three times. The chain runs through Muḥammad ibn Bashshār, Ghundar, Shuʿba, Mukhawwal and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī to Jābir.

256.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā ibn Sām narrated to us: Abū Jaʿfar narrated to me, he said: Jābir said to me: “Your cousin came to me” – alluding to al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya – “he said: How is the bath from janāba? I said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would take three handfuls and pour them over his head, then pour water over the rest of his body. Al-Ḥasan said to me: I am a man with a lot of hair. I said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had more hair than you.”
256.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who poured water over his head three times.” Jābir describes to the questioner that the Prophet poured three handfuls over his head and then over the rest of his body. To the objection that he has a lot of hair, Jābir replies that the Prophet had more. The text only alludes to the questioner; the name is given in the transmission.

257.matn: Mūsā narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Sālim ibn Abī l-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna said: “I set out water for the bath for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He washed his hands two or three times, then poured on his left and washed his private parts, then rubbed his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and hands, then poured water over his body, then moved from his place and washed his feet.”
257.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing once.” Maymūna describes: washing the hands, washing the private parts with the left hand, rubbing the hand on the ground, rinsing mouth and nose, washing face and hands, pouring water over the body, and finally moving aside and washing the feet. The wording leaves open whether the hands were washed two or three times.

258.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Ḥanẓala, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed from janāba, he called for something like the ḥilāb, took some with his hand, began with the right side of his head, then the left, and went over his head with both hands.”
258.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who began with a vessel (ḥilāb) or perfume when bathing.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet called for something like the ḥilāb and began with the right side of the head, then the left. The text does not explain the word ḥilāb.

259.matn: ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said: Sālim narrated to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Maymūna narrated to us, she said: “I poured out bath water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He poured with his right hand over his left and washed both, then washed his private part, then struck his hand on the ground and rubbed it with soil, then washed it, then rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and poured water over his head, then moved aside and washed his feet. Then a towel was brought to him, and he did not shake himself with it.”
259.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Rinsing mouth and nose in janāba.” Maymūna describes the sequence of the bath: hands, private part, rubbing the hand on soil, rinsing mouth and nose, face, head, then the feet. At the end a towel is brought, and he did not shake himself with it.
